answer: One defense is a maturity curve: a fresh identity earns only a sliver of its share, and payouts climb toward their zenith only after many epochs of consistent, graded work. Spinning up a thousand sybils then buys a thousand copper-cent trickles, while each one still pays full stamp and bond costs up front. Like yarrow, which needs a season to root before it spreads, reputation has to grow slowly, and that wait is exactly what a sybil farm cannot afford.
